name: Authentication & Secrets
description: Captured credentials, hashes, authentication outcomes and HTTP authorization schemes. Surfaces brute-force activity, plaintext-credential exposure and weak hashing.

charts.title: Captured Credentials by Service
charts.description: Which services leak credentials on the wire (HTTP, FTP, POP3, SMB, RADIUS, …). Anything other than encrypted services is a critical leak that should be remediated.

charts.title: Hash Types Observed
charts.description: Distribution of hash schemes captured (NTLMv2, Kerberos AS-REP, MD5, …). Highlights weak schemes (LM, MD5) that can be cracked with commodity hardware.

charts.title: Authentication Success vs Failure
charts.description: Ratio of successful to failed authentication events. A high failure share is a strong indicator of password-spraying or credential-stuffing campaigns.

charts.title: Top Usernames
charts.description: Most-frequent usernames seen in authentication traffic. Familiar admin / service accounts (admin, root, svc_*) appearing here are common targets for guessing attacks.

charts.title: Authentication Attempts Over Time
charts.description: Auth-attempt counts per record. Bursts correlate with credential-stuffing windows; a flat baseline indicates routine auth traffic.

charts.title: HTTP Authorization Schemes
charts.description: Authorization header schemes seen on HTTP (Bearer, Basic, Digest, NTLM, …). Basic over plain HTTP is a critical credential leak; NTLM exposure enables Pass-the-Hash.
